title: Basin imperial-remnant corridor-and-clearance skeleton
scope: Qualitative corridor-and-clearance pattern for the withdrawn power's surviving physical works in and near the initial basin; names, maps, counts, positions, ownership, law, institutions, story events, character knowledge, ancient-doorway facts, and every System-facing property remain open or excluded.
approval_evidence: On 2026-08-17 the Author selected 'Option A — CORRIDOR-AND-CLEARANCE SKELETON' by explicit multiple-choice selection, adopting the proposal's shared claim set unchanged and directing one cross-cite: the second settlement's imperial-remnant industrial village nucleus (WLD-LOCATION-005) is an instance of this record's reused-node class.
question: What qualitative pattern should govern the withdrawn power's surviving physical works in and near the initial basin — the arrangement of remnant routes, clearances, structures, water-and-ground works, and boundary or administrative traces, their condition classes, and how salvage relates to them as an activity class — without fixing names, maps, counts, positions, ownership, law, institutions, story events, character knowledge, ancient-doorway facts, or any System-facing property of any remnant?
selection: Use A — Corridor-and-clearance skeleton. The dominant surviving signature is linear: a decayed engineered route network and the broad cleared lines of the former power's organised ecological suppression lattice the lower basin and its approaches, with ruinous waystation-type and watch-type shells, scattered drainage and ground works, and occasional boundary and marker traces. Most of the skeleton is regrown, shells are ruinous, a few stretches or nodes are reused, and some stretches are avoided for practical reasons. The proposal's shared claim set applies unchanged. By Author direction, the imperial-remnant industrial village nucleus of the second settlement (WLD-LOCATION-005) is an instance of this record's reused-node class, with WLD-LOCATION-005 holding authority for everything about that settlement. Regrowth, ruin, reuse, and avoidance are condition classes, not selected events, positions, or guarantees; the settlement road's possible imperial derivation stays open, and the ancient doorways stay excluded.
alternatives: A — CORRIDOR-AND-CLEARANCE SKELETON: The dominant surviving signature is linear — a decayed engineered route network and the broad cleared lines of the former power's organised ecological suppression lattice the lower basin and its approaches, with ruinous waystation-type and watch-type shells, scattered drainage and ground works, and occasional boundary and marker traces. Most of the skeleton is regrown, shells are ruinous, a few nodes are reused by present communities, and some stretches are avoided for practical reasons. Salvage is dispersed and low-yield: worked stone and fittings from many small ruins — finite, diminishing, contestable. Selected.

B — NUCLEUS-AND-SPOKES: The dominant surviving signature is nodal — one substantial derelict administrative, garrison, and works nucleus at a relational-only distance from the settlement, with decayed spoke routes radiating toward the basin's former working landscape. The nucleus is ruinous and partly avoided because a large derelict complex is genuinely dangerous; reuse is expedition salvage — higher-yield but higher-risk and higher-cost than local quarrying. Not selected.

C — DISPERSED SMALL WORKS: The dominant surviving signature is granular — many minor installations scattered through the basin sharing workmanship, materials, and placement logic, with no single large complex; at least one is flooded or lake-claimed, expressly not at or near the WLD-LOCATION-003 staging place or spurs. Salvage is broad and shallow: many small sources, quickly exhausted, none worth organised expedition. Not selected.
rationale: The selected pattern is the most direct forward extension of the foundation capture, which already lists abandoned imperial clearances and corridors among the rewilding mosaic's elements; it distributes remnant texture across the whole basin where every accepted ecology and location record can touch it, rather than concentrating story gravity in one dungeon-like destination, and keeps the strongest questions — corridor reoccupation, road derivation, salvage friction — open at useful pressure.
evidence: Author multiple-choice selection on 2026-08-17 of 'Option A — CORRIDOR-AND-CLEARANCE SKELETON', with the shared claim set and the directed WLD-LOCATION-005 reused-node cross-cite.
consequences: Physical remnants of the withdrawn power exist in and near the initial basin, recognised by present inhabitants as that power's work by workmanship, materials, and scale — cultural recognition, not accurate functional knowledge.
The dominant surviving signature is a decayed linear skeleton: engineered route segments and suppression clearances, with small ancillaries, drainage and ground works, and boundary traces.
Present condition spans four qualitative classes: mostly regrown; shells ruinous; a few stretches or nodes reused; some avoided for practical reasons.
Legibility is partial; no complete route or clearance line is known to survive.

Up to roughly seventy years of decay, accumulating from each work's own local abandonment in the cascading retreat, degrade every surviving work; partial incidental usefulness is the ceiling, and no work is continuously occupied since abandonment.
No remnant grants working machinery, intact knowledge stores, functioning mechanisms, or preserved archives by default; any exception is a new, separately argued proposal, never an implication.
Salvage is dispersed and low-yield with finite, diminishing, contestable value; no salvage right, ownership, law, institution, market, price, or named practice exists.

Some regrown cleared ground qualitatively coincides with ground crown herds and travellers move through; no stretch is identified, no WLD-ECOLOGY-004 corridor or secondary path is located, and clearances are not claimed to cause or anchor route fidelity.
Whether the settlement's constructed road reuses any imperial-era alignment or foundation is deliberately left open.

No remnant exists at the WLD-GEOGRAPHY-002 outlet reach, at the WLD-LOCATION-003 staging place or spurs, or in any WLD-LOCATION-001 settlement zone; the constructed road corridor is excluded from this bar.
WLD-LOCATION-002 remains the sole authority for its broad fair-weather whole-journey anchors; no remnant creates a travel band, route, shortcut, or journey claim.
Regrown cleared lines are ordinary WLD-ECOLOGY-005 mosaic openings, browsed per WLD-ECOLOGY-001; no organism, reserve-web patch, or colony is placed in any remnant.

The second settlement's imperial-remnant industrial village nucleus is an instance of the reused-node class; WLD-LOCATION-005 is the authority for everything about that settlement, and this record neither locates nor describes it beyond the class relationship.

Skeleton, route segment, suppression clearance, waystation-type, watch-type, marker trace, reuse, avoidance, and salvage are author-facing qualitative labels fixing no in-world name, measurement, count, position, standard, institution, entitlement, or guarantee.
The ancient doorways stay excluded, the parked sapient pack species stays parked and unconnected, and no story event, character fact, or plot use is created.
The skeleton is author-side spatial truth and does not become automatic character knowledge of any remnant's location, condition, origin, or value.

All remnants are ordinary made things under ordinary physics and CAL0; no safe zone, spawn point, dungeon, Mana source, System structure, doorway, readout, mechanic, movement effect, map revelation, free resource, guaranteed recovery, or CAL0 change is created.
residual_unknowns: Where any remnant lies relative to the settlement, road, lake, corridor, outlet, or any accepted feature remains open, beyond the stated qualitative exclusions, pending gated WLD-GEOGRAPHY-001 mapping work.
Whether the settlement's constructed road reuses an imperial alignment, foundation, or materials remains its own future Author decision.
Whether, where, and why crown-herd movement coincides with former cleared lines, and every aspect of the WLD-ECOLOGY-004 route-fidelity mechanism, remain open.
What each work was originally for, the accuracy of present beliefs, and what records, traditions, or scholarly theories exist remain open.
All salvage practice — technique, parties, seasons, yields, rights, disputes, law, trade in salvaged material, and institutions — remains open; none exists.
Construction detail — materials, styles, inscriptions, readability by any present person — and the local collapse chronology of abandonment order and timing remain open.
Wildlife and flora relations to specific remnants remain open.
Whether any remnant preserves anything exceptional remains open, only through future separately argued proposals.
Names, terminology, cultural meaning, maps, measurements, history, character knowledge, beliefs, and misunderstandings remain open.
Mana properties, Skills, levels, settlement features, ancient-doorway relationships, offworld influence, and all other System interpretations remain open.
reopening_conditions: Later gated mapping work cannot support any coherent basin-wide linear skeleton that respects the stated exclusions at the outlet reach, staging place and spurs, and settlement zones.
Later accepted history work contradicts local-abandonment decay accumulation rather than refining its open order and timing.
Later accepted ecology makes every coherent regrown-clearance pattern contradict WLD-ECOLOGY-001 or WLD-ECOLOGY-005, or forces identification of a clearance with the WLD-ECOLOGY-004 corridor.
Later accepted work on the second settlement cannot sustain its nucleus as an instance of the reused-node class.
Later accepted salvage, culture, or institution work contradicts the dispersed low-yield salvage class rather than extending it.
The Author explicitly chooses another remnant pattern.
